## Offline re-score of the recorded live run against the corrected false-accept bar

Zero model calls. Re-scored `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` through
`provider_parity.recheck_recorded`, before and after the fix.

### Correction chosen: keep the name, fix the computation

`false_accept` is now `blocked / safe` (the false-positive rate over gold-safe items), NOT
`not-blocked / safe`. Both comparison directions (`parity.py` non-inferiority rise check and the
`max_false_accept` ceiling) are UNCHANGED — they were already written for an error rate. Cited
grounds that this is the meaning the repo already holds: `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:399,491`
(`false_accept = wrongly-fired / must-not-fire`, computed as `fp / n_nofire`);
`docs/plan-review-gate.md:382` release threshold `false_accept: 0.0`;
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml:75` "candidate false-accept rises by
<= 2pp"; and `parity.py`'s own `max_false_accept: float = 0.10` default.

Direct evidence the old computation made the ceiling always-fail: the new prerequisite test, run
against the UNFIXED source, produced `prerequisite false acceptance 1.000 exceeds 0.100` on a
candidate that wrongly blocked ZERO safe items.

### Per-slot verdict, before vs after

| slot | metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| standard | false_accept v1 -> v2 | 0.786 -> 0.786 (PASS) | 0.214 -> 0.214 (PASS) |
| standard | other failures | 1 decision flip | 1 decision flip |
| frontier | false_accept v1 -> v2 | 0.786 -> 0.929, **FAIL** "rose 0.143" | 0.214 -> 0.071, **PASS** |
| frontier | other failures | agreement 0.929 < 0.95; 2 flips | agreement 0.929 < 0.95; 2 flips |

Validity 1.000/1.000, error rate 0.000, n_gold 28 on both slots, unchanged.

**The frontier false-accept failure CLEARS.** Under the corrected metric Bedrock's false-positive
rate on gold-safe items is 0.071 vs direct Anthropic's 0.214 — a 14.3pp IMPROVEMENT, which the old
inverted computation reported as a 14.3pp regression. That is the two gold-ADVISORY cases
(`FP-rename-all-callsites-updated`, `FP-create-index-concurrently`) Anthropic false-fired on and
Bedrock did not.

### What still fails — the bar is NOT met

Both slots still fail. Standard: 1 decision flip. Frontier: 2 decision flips plus verdict agreement
0.929 below the 0.95 floor. No reinterpretation of the bar is offered; as written it is unmet.

comments.body:
## Follow-on found by the suite: a fixture had ENCODED the inverted metric

The full default selection surfaced one real consequence of the fix, now included in the same
commit.

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py` builds the prerequisite-packing gold set. It
labelled the `attribution-confusion` and `multi-bin` conflicts `"advisory"` — i.e. gold-SAFE —
while the comment directly above them said they "must still be blocked, never shipped". Those
two statements contradict each other: an `advisory` gold label means the item should NOT be
blocked.

That contradiction was only survivable while `false_accept` counted NOT-blocked safe items. The
fixture blocks all of them, so the old inverted metric scored 0.000 and cleared the 0.10 ceiling.
Under the corrected metric the same fixture reports `prerequisite false acceptance 1.000 exceeds
0.100` — which is the fixture being wrong, not the fix.

Relabelled to what the fixture actually means: every CONFLICT block is must-block (recall gold),
every CONSISTENT block is must-not-block (false-accept gold).

Measured effect — the false-accept lane goes from vacuous to real:

* gold safe items: 8 (all of them must-block, mislabelled) -> 16 (genuinely safe)
* `n_gold`: 8 -> 24 (`min_gold` for this eval is 8, so still satisfied)
* recall 1.000, false_accept 0.000 on the clean fixture
* injecting 3 wrongly-blocked safe items now trips `prerequisite false acceptance 0.188 exceeds
  0.100`, which under the old metric it could never have done

`_prerequisite_corpus` itself is untouched, so `prerequisite_corpus_digest` is unchanged and no
recorded baseline is invalidated.

This is worth noting beyond this ticket: the inverted metric had propagated into how at least one
gold set was labelled, so the labels were bent to fit the broken metric rather than the metric to
the labels.

# `parity._recall_false_accept` computes specificity but the gate fails when it RISES

## Context / Problem

`parity._recall_false_accept` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:70-82`) computes, over the gold items whose
label is NOT `block`, the fraction the runner did NOT block:

    safe = [r for r in gold if r.label != "block"]
    false_accept = sum(1 for r in safe if r.decision != "block") / len(safe) if safe else 0.0

That is SPECIFICITY (the true-negative rate) — higher is better. It is then consumed at two sites as
if it were an ERROR rate, lower-is-better:

* `parity.py:125` — `if (fa2 - fa1) > NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN + 1e-9:` reports "false-accept rose", so
  a candidate is FAILED for false-firing LESS than the baseline.
* `parity.py:252` — `if false_accept > max_false_accept + 1e-9:` against
  `max_false_accept: float = 0.10` (`parity.py:230`). Any competent gate has specificity far above
  0.10, so this comparison is effectively always-fail.

The docstring at `parity.py:71` ("false-accept = wrongly-shipped / safe") matches neither the
computation nor either consumption site.

Measured impact (story 0d76): the frontier slot of the live Bedrock provider-parity run failed partly
on `false-accept rose 0.143 > margin 0.02`, v1 0.786 -> v2 0.929. Those 0.143 are exactly two
gold-ADVISORY cases (2/14) that direct Anthropic FALSE-FIRED on and Bedrock did not. The strictly more
accurate candidate was penalised. Recorded at
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`.

## Approach

Keep the NAME `false_accept` and correct the COMPUTATION to the actual false-positive rate over safe
items — `sum(1 for r in safe if r.decision == "block") / len(safe)` — leaving both comparison
directions at `parity.py:125` and `parity.py:252` unchanged, and rewriting the docstring to describe
what is now computed.

Rationale for choosing this over renaming to `specificity` and inverting both comparisons: the
lower-is-better reading is the one the rest of the repository already encodes, so correcting the
computation makes four independent existing artifacts agree instead of requiring all of them to
change.

* `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:399` documents rebar's `false_accept` as
  "wrongly-fired / total must-not-fire fixtures (`expect` == pass)", and `eval.py:491` computes it as
  `(fp / n_nofire)` where `fp` counts `expected == "no_fire" and observed == "fire"` (`eval.py:481`).
  That is exactly `decision == "block"` over safe items. The project already has one settled meaning
  for this metric name.
* `docs/plan-review-gate.md:382` states the release thresholds as `recall: 1.0`, `false_accept: 0.0`
  — a target of 0.0 is only coherent for a lower-is-better error rate.
* `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml:75` reads
  `false_accept_margin: 0.02  # candidate false-accept rises by <= 2pp vs baseline`.
* `parity.py:230`'s `max_false_accept: float = 0.10` default and the `baseline_false_accept`
  regression check at `parity.py:260` are both written as ceilings on an error rate.

Renaming to `specificity` would instead require changing the metrics key, the two comparison
directions, the container eval tolerance, the gate doc, and the `prerequisite_fidelity_report`
keyword arguments `max_false_accept` / `baseline_false_accept` — a wider blast radius that would also
leave `parity`'s metric name disagreeing with `evals/eval.py`'s. The narrow computation fix is the
one that converges the codebase on a single definition.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — correct the `false_accept` expression in `_recall_false_accept`
  (`:81`) and rewrite the docstring at `:71-72`. No comparison operator changes.
* `tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py` — add direction-pinning tests.
* Existing assertions elsewhere that read a parity `false_accept` value are re-checked and updated
  where the corrected computation changes the expected number.

## Testing

* Happy/direction test: a candidate that false-fires on FEWER safe items than the baseline must NOT
  produce a "false-accept rose" gating failure.
* Failure-direction test: a candidate that false-fires on MORE safe items than the baseline by more
  than the 2pp margin MUST produce that gating failure.
* Boundary test: a perfect run (no safe item blocked) yields `false_accept == 0.0`, matching the
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md:382` release threshold, rather than the pre-fix `1.0`.
* `prerequisite_fidelity_report` test: a candidate blocking no safe item passes the
  `max_false_accept = 0.10` ceiling; one blocking a quarter of them fails it.
* Each new test is verified RED before the change and GREEN after, and mutation-checked in both
  directions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_recall_false_accept` returns the fraction of safe gold items the runner DID block; verified by
      a unit test asserting an exact value on a hand-built record set.
- [ ] The docstring at `parity.py:71` describes that quantity, with no reference to "wrongly-shipped";
      verified by reading the diff.
- [ ] Both consumption sites (`parity.py:125`, `parity.py:252`) keep their existing greater-than
      direction and are now correct for the computed quantity; verified by the two direction tests
      above, each failing before the change.
- [ ] A candidate that false-fires LESS than the baseline is not failed by this criterion, and one
      that false-fires more by >2pp is; verified by the two direction tests.
- [ ] The recorded provider-parity results at
      `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` are re-scored offline against the
      corrected bar with zero model calls, and whether the frontier slot's verdict changes is recorded
      as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, and the default test selection is green.
